d: Create a character, finish the tutorial on Ancora, build a raft to the Safe House and take your first tasks from K

sec.x: Every new character starts on Ancora — the tutorial island that teaches the first survival steps. Once your Raft is finished you sail to the Safe House, your first base. From there you head out to your Tamed Island and the other islands. Escape raft

Create up to 3 characters per account Watch the prologue or press Skip Pick your character's former job at creation — it gives starting skills and items Learn the basics on Ancora: scanning, gathering, resting, eating Build a raft and depart for the Safe House Take tasks from K and the beginner pioneer tasks that pay T Stone Tap other players to view their profile, message them, or invite them to a party/clan

Launch the game → Select Server (the server list is shown in game · see Picking a server) → Create Character Set your appearance, then pick your character's former job in the prologue — it hands out starting skills and items on your first login (see Skills & jobs) You can Skip the opening scene One account holds 3 characters — characters waiting to be deleted still count Deleting a character: it is removed for real after a 24-hour countdown, which you can cancel · a character that is online cannot be deleted For logging in and moving to another PC see Account & login

New characters spawn on Ancora. The guide pops up step by step, and the tasks (the "Ancora" group) run in order: Step   Task   Goal   Reward 1   Try the scan button   Press the magnifier button in the screen corner   30 EXP 2   Logs for the raft   Have 4 Logs   40 EXP 3   Stalks to bind the raft   Have 6 Stalks   40 EXP 4   Leave Ancora   Put the materials into the raft on the beach and depart to the Safe House   120 EXP · 500 T Stone Make a Raft Make a Raft: touch the raft on the beach → put in 4 Logs + 6 Stalks → when complete press Depart Depart → you land at the Safe House The raft is the only way off Ancora — sailing any other way before the raft is done is refused During the tutorial K gives you emergency rations (if you have nothing edible in your bag) The date palms for the food task grow new fruit in 5 seconds, so nobody gets stuck waiting If you log out mid-tutorial you come back to the same spot on Ancora What's at each tutorial spot — Ancora's resources were rebuilt to match the original game. Everything is on ground you can walk to; nothing sits on cliffs or unreachable plateaus. Spot   What you'll find Old railroad cars   Date palms · 2 small Compsognathus (scenery) The stream   Reeds The lakeshore   Stones · reeds (the Brachiosaurus stay in the lake — none walk on land) The bonfire   Branches · stones The small lake by the raft   Trees for logs · reeds Resting at the bonfire on Ancora empties your Fatigue in 5 seconds (only bonfires on this island · Life/Health

The tutorial's axe step uses the Improvised One-Handed Axe recipe, which is unlocked from the moment you create your character — no skill level and no bone/skull needed. Put in a Stone Blade (made from stones) + a Reed Stalk + a branch to get an Improvised Stone Axe, then chop trees for the raft logs. Characters created before this change get the recipe automatically on their next login [!tip] No axe yet? Look for fallen logs on the ground, and reeds along the stream or the lakes.

sec.h: 3. The Safe House — your first base
sec.x: The raft always lands you at the Safe House's entry point (the Company's rest island). It is a safe island: no fatigue from climate or island level, and the weather is mostly sunny (see Weather). If you log in stuck in deep water and can't move (on any island), the server moves you to the island's entry point · a return point left in deep water is cleared, so dying takes you to the entry point instead · players on land, beaches or shallow water stay where they are What you can do at the Safe House: Talk to K to get the "Tasks from K" chain Take the balloon to pick your own Tamed Island — choose 1 of 5 maps, once (see Choosing your Tamed Island layout) Sail to other islands from the port (see Travel) It is the default return point when the island you were on is not stable (see Death) Tasks from K Task   Goal   Reward Report to K   Talk to K next to her motorbike   50 EXP Firewood for K   Gather 5 items from the trees around the Safe House, then talk to K   120 EXP · 300 T Stone A stone knife for K   Make 1 stone knife and bring it to K   200 EXP · 500 T Stone Stone knife

These can be done anywhere, in any order: Task   Goal   Reward Gatherer   Gather 20 items from nature   60 EXP · 200 T Stone Apprentice   Craft your first item   60 EXP · 200 T Stone Building a home   Build your first structure   80 EXP · 300 T Stone Hunter   Hunt 3 animals   80 EXP · 300 T Stone First friend   Tame 1 animal   100 EXP · 500 T Stone A pioneer's first step   Reach level 5   1,000 T Stone After these, a long story chain runs up to level 60 — see Tasks & story.

A new character receives a welcome mail — the first character of an account gets 300 T Stone attached (characters 2–3 get the text only). Update-news mails with attachments are also paid once per account. See Mail.

On screen   Meaning   Read more Life   Your HP — at zero you die   Death Health   The ceiling of your Life   Survival Stamina / Energy   Power for running/fighting · Energy is refilled by eating   Eating Fatigue   Too high and you cannot work — rest   Survival Status icons   Buffs/debuffs you have (Wet, Washed, Full…)   Survival Mail icon   Rewards and news   Mail [!tip] Finish K's tasks and the beginner tasks before going far — together they pay several thousand T Stone to start with.

Tapping another player's character opens a menu: Button   What it does View Profile   Their name, level and clan Message   Opens a private two-person chat · players who block each other can't message Invite to Party   Greyed out if you are a member (not the leader), the party is full (8), or they are already in another party Invite to Clan   Shown only when your clan rank can invite and they have no clan Report   Tell the team — type /report reason in chat after tapping that player (within 10 minutes), or /report <character name> <reason> · you can report the same player once a day · the server's reply is in Thai Tapping a downed character still gives CPR as before (Death)

d: Your character's path step by step, from the first island to end-game content — what to do in each stage, with links to the detailed pages

sec.x: This page puts things in a sensible order, from creating a character to end-game content · Numbers and button steps are on each system's page (links at the end of each stage) · You can skip ahead — nothing forces this order
Pick a server in-game, then link Discord to get a transfer key so you never lose your character — Account & Login The server is still in testing — see what isn't finished on Roadmap to launch

sec.h: Stage 1 — Day one: Ancora → Safe House
sec.x: Create a character and pick a former career (you get starting skills and items for it) On Ancora, follow the tasks in order: scan → 4 logs → 6 stalks → build the raft and depart Land at the Safe House, talk to K, do the missions from K (firewood · stone knife) and the New Pioneer tasks that pay T-Stones Read more: Getting Started · Quests and Rewards [!tip] The early tasks pay enough T-Stones for your first essentials — don't spend it all at once

Watch the Life · Health · Energy · Fatigue gauges — when you're tired, rest near a bonfire or under a roof Drink water, wash, and eat (you can't spam food — there is hidden fullness) Mind your body temperature on hot/cold islands When you die, half of your bag drops at the death spot — go back for it quickly Read more: Survival · Eating and drinking · Buffs and status effects · Death & Revival

sec.h: Stage 3 — Gathering and your first tools
sec.x: Gather wood, stone and plants by hand first, then craft an axe, hammer and knife for things that need tools Your tool's level must be at least the island's level to gather there — upgrade tools for the islands you visit Gathered items can carry latent/rare attributes that pass on to what you craft Read more: Gathering · Crafting · Weapons and tools · Materials · Item attributes

At the Safe House, take the balloon to the Tamed Island — you pick the island layout once · the Tamed Island is one shared world, you can see your friends' homes · there are no wild animals on it · the Supporter role gets a private Tamed Island and chooses who may enter Declare a Domain of your own, then expand it — things inside your Domain decay much more slowly than outside Build a house, storage boxes, workbenches and a bonfire Give friends permissions to use your things if you want Read more: Islands & Travel · Domain · Building · Storage · Decay and repair [!warn] Structures outside a Domain disappear quickly — keep valuables inside your own Domain

Make farm plots, sow seeds, water, fertilize, harvest Cook at a bonfire/kitchen for buffs and taste Fresh food spoils — smoke, dry, pickle or can it to keep it Read more: Farming · Cooking · Preserving food · Food, drinks and medicine

Learn to hit with the right moves and directions, butcher carcasses for meat, hide and bone Bring an animal to low health or stun it, capture it with a taming herb → train it in a pen → form a bond Pets fight with you, carry you and your cargo, and produce milk Read more: Combat · Wild animals · Taming · Pets

Every action gives character EXP and skill-category EXP · the character level cap is 99 · spend Skill Points on new skills, rewind a limited number per day Swap gear as you level, repair it when worn, dye it Wear a title earned from the Career Guide, organizations and levels Read more: Skills and Careers · Skill list · Character stats · Equipment and repair · Clothing and accessories · Titles

Sail from a harbor to Unstable Islands of each climate — higher-level islands have stronger animals and tire you faster The Unstable Index makes islands harsher — you need enough Climate Resistance before you go Explore the map for warp holes, craters and rifts to earn T-Stones · unlock the quick-warp buttons Read more: Islands & Travel · Weather & Unstable Index · Map and exploration · Warps & Rifts

sec.h: Stage 9 — Organizations, routines and the economy
sec.x: Do missions and support requests for organizations to raise Trust and earn T-Stones and titles Do Weekly Tasks for pioneer points, and check in daily for attendance rewards Trade with players on the market, send items home through a Courier Warp Hole, collect things from your mailbox Read more: Organizations · Quests and Rewards · Market and Shop · Transport and Vehicles · Mail · Traps and wells

Team up in a clan to share land and boxes, and form alliances Take on Rifts and the Warp Accelerator with friends for tiered rewards (there is a weekly cap) Reach the high-Index islands, collect gear with rare attributes, build a full set of pets Try the Lawless Islands (Lv56 and up) — you can attack other players, and whatever drops when someone dies is anyone's to pick up Follow upcoming systems on Roadmap to launch Read more: Clans · Warps & Rifts · Lawless Islands (PvP) · Items

d: The CBT server is open to everyone · link Discord with the in-game Link Discord button or a bot code · move to a new PC · one PC per account at a time · the Supporter role gives extra perks

sec.x: Your game account is tied to your device (the installed game) automatically — on first launch you can create a character and play right away. Linking Discord gives you a first-time gift, a device transfer key for moving to a new PC, and lets the game know you have the Supporter role. There is no password to remember.

Pick a server from the list in game — right now the CBT server is open to everyone Link your account to Discord with the in-game Link Discord button or a 6-character bot code — the first link mails you 100 T Stone + a transfer key Move to a new PC / reinstall with the Link Discord button or your transfer key and get your characters back Get a new key when yours is lost or leaked (the old one stops working immediately) Delete a character or your account, with time to change your mind Supporter role: skip the queue · separate entrance · private Tamed Island

The server list is shown in game on the Select Server screen — the launcher (DurangoLauncher) is only for updating the game; you do not need it every time (starting the game directly works too). There is now a single server, CBT (CloseBeta), and it is open to everyone — no Discord link or role needed · the Prebeta server has closed (29 Sep 2026). Button in the server list   Who uses it [CBT]   Everyone [CBT] Supporter   Separate entrance for players with the Supporter role · players without the role can press it too, but they join the same queue as [CBT] and go in the normal way Both buttons lead to the same world — the same account and characters; you see each other and can party, clan and use the Market together · if one entrance has trouble, the server sends you through the other one automatically When it is busy the server may open a login queue — the Supporter role skips it on either button

There are 2 ways with the same result — your first link sends  a mail from Discord with  100 T Stone and your device transfer key. Way 1 — the Link Discord button in game (game version 3.0.0 or newer) In game: Settings ▸ Account ▸ Link Discord → your browser opens a Discord page Press Authorize on the Discord page → back to the game, done — no code needed The button changes to your Discord name with a ✓ · if you are not in our Discord server yet, you are added automatically This account is already linked to another Discord → the game asks before switching The Discord you authorize belongs to your old account on another PC → the game asks you to confirm, then moves your characters to this PC (see the next section) Way 2 — a code from the bot On the server's Discord press the 🔗 link button → the bot opens a private channel with a 6-character code In game: Settings ▸ Account ▸ Enter Coupon ▸ type the code On success you get the same mail as Way 1 · the bot's private channel shows the key too (the channel is deleted within 10 minutes — write the key down) Item   Value Bot code   6 characters · valid 10 minutes · single use Characters used   A–Z and 2–9 (no 0 O 1 I, to avoid mix-ups) First-link gift   100 T Stone (by mail) — once per Discord account, whichever way you link · unlinking and linking again only sends the key Linked before the key system existed? The key mail arrives the next time you log in. You can't unlink in game — type /unlink on Discord

sec.h: Moving to a new PC / reinstalling
sec.x: Install the game on the new PC and log in (a throwaway character is fine), then use either way: Link Discord button: Settings ▸ Account ▸ Link Discord → authorize with your old Discord → the game shows your old account's character names to confirm → OK Transfer key: Settings ▸ Account ▸ Enter Coupon ▸ type your transfer key (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX) Then Return to Title and log in again = your account's characters are back. Item   Value Key format   12 characters (XXXX-XXXX-XXXX), same character set as the bot code Game version   Link Discord button 3.0.0 or newer · transfer key 2.8.2 or newer (update through DurangoLauncher) Whenever your account is moved to another PC, the bot DMs you and a new key is issued Lost or leaked key: link with the Link Discord button, or press 🔗 for a new code and enter it from your PC = you move instantly and get a new key · or press 🔑 New key in the bot's ticket channel (once per minute) — the old key dies at once Since game version 3.0.0, clicking the red account-number row on the Account tab no longer opens the code screen — use one of the two ways above There are no passwords any more [!warn] Your transfer key is like a house key — anyone who has it can move your account to their PC. Never share it.

sec.h: One PC per account at a time
sec.x: An account plays one character on one PC at a time — if you log in from another PC (or with another character of the same account), the one already online is disconnected · this applies across both [CBT] and [CBT] Supporter.

Deletion   Time before it is gone   How to cancel Delete character (character select screen)   24 hours   Cancel the deletion on the character select screen Delete account (Settings ▸ Account)   7 days   Log in / create a character / cancel the deletion within 7 days = the whole account is restored Characters waiting to be deleted still count toward the 3-per-account limit Deleting the account also unlinks Discord [!tip] To see your full account number, type /myaccount on Discord (only you can see the reply).

d: Life, Health, Energy and Fatigue gauges · resting, drinking and washing · body temperature and getting too cold or too hot

sec.x: Every island in Durango wears you down — fatigue piles up from work and climate, walking burns Energy, and your body temperature follows the weather. This page explains the gauges on screen, how to recover, and the server's real numbers.

Rest next to a shelter or bonfire to lower Fatigue and recover Life Drink Water and Wash at the water's edge to ease heat fatigue Draw Water into a container for later Eat to refill Energy (details in Eating) Get out of the rain into a house/tent, warm up at a fire, eat hot/cold food, wear weather-resistant gear to control your body temperature Log out to rest — time offline counts as resting

Gauge   Starting maximum   Changes over time   Notes Life   Equal to your Health   +60/min   At zero you die (Death) Health   300 (+4 per level above 1)   +4.2/hour   The ceiling of Life · drops while you are too cold/too hot Stamina   Equal to your Energy   +5/second   Used for running/fighting Energy   100 (+1.5 per level above 1)   +16.7/hour · walking −1.9/min   Refill by eating · the ceiling of Stamina Fatigue   0–100   Does not drop by itself while online   Rises from work, climate, weather · drops by resting When you lack the Energy for an action, the game asks whether to go on anyway

sec.x: The gauge ceilings and regeneration speeds on screen add up every source — the numbers on the stats window always match the gauges on screen Source   Examples Skills   Health I–VI +250 Max Health in total · Bulk Up +10 Max Energy per step · Life Recovery I–VI +1/second in total (Life regenerates at 2/second) · Stamina Recovery I–VI +2.5/second in total (Stamina regenerates at 7.5/second) Worn items   The stats written on the item (e.g. some event items give +90 Max Health) and the item's attributes — see Clothing and accessories Food   Enhanced Ability buffs (Eating and drinking) Titles   The stats of the title you are using (Titles) House moods   Cute Ambiance +70 Max Energy · +0.15 Energy/second (Buffs) Endurance above 10 adds 2 Max Health per point · Will above 10 adds 0.8 Max Energy per point — points from every source count (base, worn items, food) When Max Health rises, your current value rises with it (like a level-up) · Max Energy gained from skills/items/houses only widens the gauge — eat or rest to fill it When a ceiling drops (you take an item off, a buff ends), anything above it is cut down to the ceiling Items at zero durability give no stats (Equipment and repair) Fatigue low   Fatigue maxed The on-screen fatigue icons, from fine to exhausted

sec.h: Timed actions one at a time
sec.x: Drinking, washing, drawing water and every other action with a progress bar (gathering, butchering, dyeing, taming, Look Around, crafting …) run one at a time Starting a new one before the current bar is full cancels the old one, which gives nothing · mashing the button only gives the last one Drinking and washing apply when the bar is full · washing at a bathtub needs you to still be next to it when the bar fills Durations and effects (fatigue removed, energy) are unchanged · the energy for drawing water is paid at the start and not refunded if cancelled
Every food adds fullness (there is no gauge on screen). At 100 you get the Full status and cannot eat more · fullness drains from full to empty in 30 minutes — details in Eating.

There is no temperature gauge on screen — watch your character's pose (shivering when cold, a heat pose when hot) and your status icons. sec.h: Logging out on a temporary island
sec.x: In the original game unstable islands could disappear, so this server decides at login: if you log out or disconnect on a temporary island, your next login puts you at the landing point of your home island (where your waypoint is) if that island is still stable, otherwise at the Safe House, with a message that your previous island is gone. Island you logged out on   Next login Safe House · Ancora · Tamed Island · villages/cities · Index 1 islands   Same place Index 2 and up islands · event islands · training island · islands that were closed   Home island → otherwise Safe House Your items and pets all come with you Just arriving on a temporary island does not move you — only logging back in after really leaving the game does Leaving an island by any means clears your checkpoint on that island [!tip] Logging off for a long time? Do it on your home island, your Tamed Island or the Safe House — you will come back to the same spot.

Within 12 tiles of an island's port/spawn point no animals spawn or walk in, and predators do not follow you in — revive at the landing point and you will not be mobbed again. But if you hit an animal first, it can hit back from the edge of the zone while you are within its reach — see When an animal is hit

The original game had after-effects of reviving (dizziness lowering accuracy · reviving with less than full gauges if you die often) — this server does not apply them yet, and is set to always revive with full gauges.

d: Gather plants, wood, stone and ore, and butcher carcasses — item level, success chance, required tools and regrow times

sec.x: Everything on the islands starts with gathering — branches, leaves, stones and ore, all the way to leather and meat from animal carcasses. Every gathered item has a level; the higher the level, the better the things you craft from it. Some pieces also come with latent attributes. Players gathering plants and ore

Plants — leaves, fruit, flowers, reeds, mushrooms and more; most can be picked bare-handed Wood — branches and bark by hand · logs from big trees need an axe or a saw Stone and ore — big stones, ore and gems need a pickaxe or a hammer Dirt — bare hands or a shovel Carcasses — hunt an animal, then butcher it for leather, meat and bone (Butchering skill category) — see Animals Structures that produce items — such as wells or traps, harvested in rounds — see Building

Walk up to the resource (within 3 tiles) and tap it The menu lists what you can gather there, with the level you will actually get Pick an entry — the game picks a suitable tool for you; entries you have no usable tool for are grayed out Wait for the progress bar to fill, then see the result: Success · Flawless Success · or Failed to Gather If your Energy is low, the game asks whether you want to continue Some categories need a skill first — tapping them opens the skill page for the skill you need

sec.h: One timed action at a time
sec.x: Actions with a progress bar (gathering, butchering, washing, drinking, drawing water, dyeing, taming, crafting and so on) run one at a time Starting a new one before the current bar is full = the new one replaces it, and the old one gives nothing · the unfinished resource stays where it was, nothing is lost Results arrive only when the bar completes · for gathering, the resource is taken when the bar completes — if someone else takes it first or you walk out of range, you get nothing The energy/fatigue for gathering is paid when you start — it is not refunded if the action is cancelled

d: Craft tools, weapons and clothes and process materials — recipes, workbenches, success chance and failure, product level, Processing Chances and desulfurizing metal with seashells

sec.x: What you gather becomes tools, weapons, clothes, food and building parts. Many materials must be processed first (trimmed, smelted, tanned, dried …) before the next recipe accepts them. The level and attributes of your materials carry over into what you make. A recipe's material slots

Every craft is rolled against the recipe's Difficulty (shown in the Expected Result window — it grows with the product level) and your Crafting Ability in the recipe's category: gap = Difficulty − Crafting Ability   (0 when your ability is higher) success chance = 1 − (gap ÷ 100)² Result   Chance   What happens Success   1 − (gap ÷ 100)²   you get the item — it may be a Flawless Success Failure   (gap ÷ 100)² − (gap ÷ 100)³   the game shows it as a success and you get the item, but no Flawless Success and no bonus items · weapons, tools, clothes and accessories start at 70% of max durability (repair brings them back to full) · food and materials are not affected Big failure   (gap ÷ 100)³   the game says «Crafting Failed» · no item · you lose gap % of the materials, the rest go back to your bag (the same pieces) · Stamina and time are not refunded · half experience Recovery rate — mastery ladder steps in 8 crafting categories give recovery rate (+10%, +15%, +20%, +30% per step): materials lost on a big failure × (1 − recovery rate) · at most 90% recovered · Farming has none Which pieces are lost is random — per slot, count × loss share, and any fraction is a chance to lose one more piece Dyeing and bleaching recipes ignore ability and always succeed · so do recipes with no Difficulty Unattended crafting rolls when you place the job — on a big failure nothing is put on the workbench Until 24 Sep every craft succeeded; the original formula is now in use

Supported recipes (such as smelting ore and desulfurizing metal at a kiln) can be left on a Workbench — materials are taken right away and the item waits on the table until the time is up Each recipe has its own wait time (at least 5 s) · a full workbench takes no more jobs A workbench, kiln, campfire or drying rack on someone else's Domain needs all of Use + Give + Take to craft, place or collect jobs (otherwise the buttons are greyed out) — see Domain A workbench built from a material with «Splits Easily» may get «More Space» (+1 slot) or «Shorter Duration» (−5% unattended time) — see Item attributes

A weapon assembled from parts Processing doesn't turn the item into a new one — it adds tags/attributes to the same piece, and the next recipe checks those tags. d: Latent and rare (green) attributes — how you get them while gathering, how they carry over when crafting, and what each one does

sec.x: Each material may come with attributes such as «Firm», «High Density», or green ones like «Black Sheen». When you craft, the attributes of the material in the main slot become attributes of the product — more attack, more durability, or special effects like bleeding. A sword with special attributes

Open Item Info for the item Attributes show as chips  with their level — the color tells how rare they are: Color   Meaning Green   Rare Attribute — a special effect Yellow   a good attribute Normal   a basic attribute Gray   a negative attribute Tap a chip to read its description · combat/gathering rare attributes have no number on the stats page — read the chip's description instead

When you gather or butcher, each piece can get two kinds of attributes: Source attributes — some sources always give fixed attributes · the main one gets +1 level for each point of the island's Unstable Index above 1, and +1 on a Flawless gather Random latent attribute — 15% chance per piece (22.5% on a Flawless gather) · if one appears, a second roll decides whether it is green or yellow/gray Chance to be green = material + skill + gear (total capped at 90%) Part   From   Formula   Max Material   the island's Unstable Index (stable islands = 1)   5% × Index · ×2 for big-animal parts   50% Skill   Gathering category level (carcasses: Butchering)   20% × category level ÷ 60   20% Gear   the tool you gather with (bare hands = what you wear)   «Secrets of Gathering» +10% · +10% × tool level ÷ 60   20% Green level = 1 + round(chance ÷ 90% × 9) → 5% gives level 1 · 50% gives level 6 · 90% gives level 10 If not green: yellow 70% / gray 30% · level 2–3 (+1 on a Flawless gather)

Attributes that give stats — every weather resistance, Defense Buff, Attack Buff, accuracy, critical, Durability Buff, crafting/gathering skills, base stats, stealth, Storage Capacity and so on — can come two ways on the same item: From the item's design — many grow with the item's level, e.g. Winter Fur Gloves carry Cold Resistance Buff = 1 + level × 0.05 (Lv60 = 4) · fractions round half up (3.95 → 4), except Storage Capacity, which rounds down Latent attributes picked up while gathering/crafting The level that really counts = design + latent (up to that attribute's maximum level) · the item info screen shows the total · the success label after crafting/gathering shows «Lv design → Lv total» Example (1 resistance point = −3% fatigue of that kind)   Cold Resistance   Cold fatigue Winter Fur Gloves Lv60, no latent   4   −12% Same gloves + latent Cold Resistance Buff 2   6   −18% Full 5-piece winter set Lv60, no latent   24   −72% Material/structure attributes (Strong, High Density and the like that recipes check) work as before: the latent value replaces the design value · recipe requirements do not change When crafting, only the latent value carries over; the result then adds its own design value Storage Capacity (from the bag-pocket modification or latent): level = extra bag slots (Storage) An item at zero durability — none of its attributes work (resistance, immunity, capacity, buffs) until repaired · the stats window updates as soon as it breaks or is repaired Food attrib

d: Learn the seed's skill, build a plot, sow, water it fully, fertilize for more harvest — when it matures the crop survives or withers depending on water and the island's climate

sec.x: Grow your own plants on plots you build. Crops grow in real time, even while you are offline. When the growing time is up, the crop either succeeds (ready to harvest) or withers — water it fully and pick crops that suit the island's climate to keep it alive. Harvesting gives the produce (food, flowers, fiber and more) plus one seed back. Planting a seed

d: Eat to refill energy and get buffs and taste bonuses — a hidden satiety meter stops you from binge-eating

sec.x: Food is your character's main source of Energy. Besides energy, some foods restore health, give stat buffs, help against heat or cold, or boost the exp you earn when they taste good — but you can't binge-eat, because a hidden "satiety" meter holds you back. Eating

Eat food from your bag → get its full energy right away, plus the food's other effects Drink Water at a river, lake or sea shore without needing a bottle or item Eat tasty food to get the Delicious status (more exp) and foods that give the Enhanced Ability buff Cook before eating to avoid Stomach Pain from raw food (see Cooking)

Open your bag, pick a food and choose Eat (drinks: Drink) — your character plays an eating animation, then the effect applies Stand next to water and choose Drink Water — takes 5 seconds and gives +5 energy and the Water status, same as drinking a bottle of water, without using an item · the effect applies when the bar completes — starting something else during the bar cancels that drink (one at a time) If you eat a different buff food while a food buff is still active, the game asks "Previous food's effect will disappear. Continue?" — confirm and the new buff replaces the old one

There is no satiety bar on screen, but the server tracks it in the background: Every food has its own satiety value, added when you eat it Satiety caps at 100 and digests steadily, from 100 down to empty in 30 minutes While you are below 100 you can always eat, even if that bite takes you over 100 Once you reach 100 you get the Full status and can't eat; the game tells you roughly how many seconds/minutes to wait Dying or levelling up removes Full immediately Drink Water from a water source does not count toward satiety Food   Satiety per piece   Pieces until Full (from empty)   Steady rate (pieces/hour) Water   5   20   40 Apple · Minnow · Egg · Raspberry   10   10   20 Meat Kebab   12   9   16.7 Bread · Meat-Stuffed Bread · Sashimi · Root   15   7   13.3 Meat   20   5   10 Tenderloin Steak   50   2   4 Fat   120   1   1.7

With Luxurious Ambiance from a house (Buffs) your satiety drops 0.5% slower per total mood level of the house (at most 90% slower) Total mood level   Satiety drops slower by   Full to empty No mood   —   30 minutes 15   7.5%   about 32 minutes 40   20%   37.5 minutes This makes you stay full longer and eat less often — the in-game description says it shortens satiety, but this server follows the decision made for it When the buff ends or changes, satiety goes back to the normal rate from that moment (the time before is not recalculated)

All of a food's taste values (sweet, salty, savory, oily, spicy, bitter, sour) add up to one score: Taste score   Status   Effect (5 minutes) 3 or more   Delicious   Character exp from actions ×1.03 −3 or less   Horrible   More fatigue In between   —   Nothing Properties on a food item change its taste — anything with the Raw property tastes much worse (raw meat = Horrible + Stomach Pain), but cooking removes Raw, so the same meat becomes Delicious. Eating raw food also cancels Delicious.

sec.h: Effects from a food's own attributes
sec.x: Some foods carry an attribute of their own; its level grows with the item's level (fractions round half up) and it takes effect when eaten: Food   Own attribute   When eaten Mushroom   Poisonous to Humans level 1 (Lv1–9) · 2 (Lv10–29) · 3 (Lv30–49) · 4 (Lv50–69) · 5 (Lv70)   Eaten raw — including dried, smoked, pickled or canned — gives Poisoned for 1 minute: Health −(0.5 + 0.5 × level)/second = −60 to −180 in total · cooking it with fire/water/oil removes the poison and gives Hot Food instead Freshwater Eel   Stamina Food level 1–5 (same level bands as the mushroom)   Raw = Stomach Pain · cooked (skewer, boil, steam, grill, fry …) = Stamina Recovery Speed Buff at the same level for 5 minutes (instead of Hot Food) · dried/smoked/pickled = no effect Ice · Shaved Ice   Cold = item level   Cold Food at the item's level, up to 5 · Ice 5 minutes · Shaved Ice 20 minutes Barley Drink   Fatigue Debuff = item level   Quenching Drink for 5 minutes: Fatigue −0.18 × level per minute (Lv60 ≈ −54 over the 5 minutes) Dried Persimmon   Max Health, Max Energy Buff = item level   Surging Sweetness for 5 minutes: Max Health +2 × level · Max Energy +0.5 × level The item info screen shows the effect level you really get when eating (never above the status's maximum) — e.g. Lv10 Ice shows Cold Food level 5 Stat effects from food statuses (e.g. Strange Eats, Will +3) now count on your character sheet Levelling up right after eating a raw mushroom clears the poison at once Eating together

Gathering, crafting and other work cost energy. If you have less energy than an action needs, the game warns you first and lets you choose to eat first or carry on — for the energy and fatigue gauges see Survival.

[!tip] Grill meat with the Skewer recipe before eating — same energy, but no Stomach Pain and you get Delicious (exp ×1.03). [!tip] High-satiety foods (Fat, steak) fill you up fast. If you need lots of energy, pick foods with high energy but low satiety, such as Apple. [!tip] You can only have one Enhanced Ability buff at a time — don't accidentally eat a different buff food over the one you want.
The "water" value of food has no effect yet (the game has no water gauge) The Phenomenal Flavor and Disgusting statuses never happen, because the game data has no thresholds for them

d: Build houses, furniture, workbenches and boxes — pick a site, add materials, build, then maintain, repair, demolish or package them

sec.x: Player-built houses and a party yard Everything a player places on the ground — tents, houses, workbenches, bonfires, boxes, furniture — is a structure. You build it from a blueprint unlocked through skills (Skills) and fill it with materials from your bag.

Select a construction site → add materials → build (some structures then need extra time to finish) Let friends help with finalization, or pay T-Stones for instant construction Use it: open boxes, craft at workbenches, light/put out fires, open/close gates, rest in tents, name it, write on signs Houses: modify parts, change textures, place wall decorations, extend floors, complete furniture sets Repair when Durability drops (Decay and repair) · demolish to get materials back · package it and place it elsewhere

Open Structure Building and pick a blueprint you have learned (unlearned blueprints cannot be built) Select Construction Site on the ground — you must stand within 4 tiles and it must not overlap another structure Touch the site and put materials into each slot (the item's tags must match the slot) — anyone can help put materials into a site When all slots are full, press Build — some blueprints need a hammer (or saw) in your bag; the tool wears each use If the blueprint has a finishing time, the structure stays translucent with scaffolding until the time is up, then it becomes usable A structure's level = the average level of the materials you used (within the blueprint's level range) · workbenches get workbench tags capped at this level and may inherit special properties from the main material (Item tags) [!tip] Always build on your own Domain — structures outside a Domain break within 1 day and vanish if nobody uses them. See Domain and Decay [!note] Player-placed bonfires don't last long anywhere — unused for 3 minutes the fire dies out, and 1 minute after going out the bonfire vanishes (Bonfires dying out and disappearing)

Free ground not covered by another structure (discarded item bundles do not block) Not allowed: in water · on top of trees/rocks/plants that are still standing (felled ones don't block) · tiles the game marks as unbuildable · on the tutorial island — the same rules as the colored frame when you pick a site Someone else's Domain: not allowed unless the owner grants the «Build» permission (Domain) Interior furniture must sit entirely inside the frame of a finished house (not half in, half out) · in multi-floor houses you can stack furniture on different floors (upper floor above lower-floor furniture) · indoor-only items can't be placed outside

Workbenches Workbenches (kitchens, kilns, drying racks, …) are needed for workbench recipes; stand within 4 tiles. Some recipes (food, firing, drying, fertilizer) are unattended crafting — leave the job on the bench, go do something else, and collect the result when the time is up · cancelling returns the materials. See recipes in Crafting and Cooking.

House doors are wall decorations (the Basic Wooden Door Frame comes with the house · swap it for a wooden door etc. on the Wall Decoration screen). Gate-type structures can be opened/closed by touching them · on someone else's Domain you need the «Enter» permission to use the gate (this permission does not stop anyone walking into the Domain)

Touch your own structure → Demolish · wait for the bar (length depends on Durability, usually ≈ 6 seconds) · the animation follows the hammer in your hands (two-handed / one-handed / bare hands) — time and energy are the same Materials come back in proportion to Durability at the moment you demolish (badly decayed = fewer) · a site that was never built returns 100% Items in boxes/storage, reins in pens, wall decorations (doors, windows), workbench jobs (finished = the product · unfinished = materials back) and incoming cargo all go to the demolisher's bag · pets in pens go back to their owner Demolishing a house also demolishes every piece of furniture inside it (all floors) — materials and contents go to your bag, nothing is left floating Returned items enter your bag even if it is full (nothing is lost) Domain owners who touch someone else's structure on their own Domain get Demolish and Package options · demolish = materials go to the demolisher's bag · the contents are mailed back to the original builder · package = see Domain

Packageable structures: touch → Package (the owner · or the owner of the Domain it stands on — see Domain). It becomes a «Packaged Construction» item or a Moving Box in your bag. Packaging your own structure keeps everything — level, Durability, name, box contents · Durability does not drop while you carry it · place it somewhere new without rebuilding. sec.x: Private Domain flag A Domain is land a player declares as their own, made of plots of 4 × 4 tiles. Structures on your own Domain decay far more slowly (7 days and they never vanish — see Decay), and nobody else can build, demolish or open boxes there without permission.

sec.h: Farm plots and gates on a Domain
sec.x: On your Domain, others can sow, water, fertilize or uproot/harvest a farm plot only if they have all 3 permissions Use + Give + Take (or you opened that plot's own per-item permission) — without them the plot's buttons can't be pressed · whoever built the plot can always use it (Farming) Others can open/close gates on your Domain only with the «Enter» permission · walking onto the Domain is never blocked A sprinkler on someone else's Domain needs the «Use» permission

sec.h: Domain owners and other players' structures
sec.x: A Domain owner (on a clan Enclave: a rank that can manage the Enclave) who touches a structure someone else built on their Domain gets: Demolish — materials go to the demolisher's bag · the contents are mailed back to the builder Package (packageable items · free) — the package goes into the Domain owner's bag and becomes the Domain owner's (wherever you place it, it is yours) · the builder loses that structure Contents (box/storage items, wall decorations, workbench jobs, incoming cargo, reins in taming pens) do not go into the package — they are mailed back to the builder · animals in pens go back to their owners · crops in farm plots are lost (as with demolishing) A custom name and the text/drawing on a sign are cleared · incense in a censer stays · a house keeps its Basic Wooden Door Frame Packaging a house: furniture you built yourself goes back to your bag · other players' furniture is mailed back whole to whoever built it (as a package if it can be packaged, otherwise as materials by Durability + its contents) The builder always gets a notice by mail, even with nothing inside (the mail is in Thai · structure names in it are the Korean in-game names) Structures with zero Durability (repair first) or not yet finished can't be packaged — they can be demolished Packaging (moving) a structure is free on your own Domain/your clan's Enclave · elsewhere 100 × level T-Stones (Building) [!warn] Building on someone else's Domain = its owner can demolish or package your structure
In the original game a Domain expired and had to be extended — this server does not have that yet: Domains never expire and have no daily maintenance fee; they last until the owner cancels them.

d: Fight animals bare handed, with melee weapons, bows or crossbows — damage depends on attack, the move you use, and armor penetration against the animal's defense · character combat stats, auto-dodge and auto-block · fighting players on the Lawless Islands

sec.x: Dinosaurs and wild animals are your food, your materials and your biggest danger. Combat on this server follows the original game's rules: every hit starts from weapon attack × the move's multiplier, then compares your armor penetration with the animal's defense. The colored area an animal draws on the ground while winding up is exactly where it will hit — step out in time and it misses. A hunter slashing a raptor

Fight bare handed, with one-handed weapons (axe · knife/sword · blunt weapon), two-handed weapons, spears, bows and crossbows Use heavy hits, flurries and sweeping moves that hit several animals at once (these must be learned from the combat skill tree — see Skills) Stagger an animal so the attack it is winding up is cancelled; make it stunned / collapse to capture it (see Taming) Break body parts (head · body · legs · tail) to slow an animal down or weaken its attacks Use green weapon tags to make animals bleed (see Tags) On the Lawless Islands (level 56+) you can fight other players — see Lawless Islands (PvP)

Tap an animal to target it, then press Attack  — your character walks into range and swings A weapon's basic attack is always available · special moves (heavy hit, flurry, stab, sweep, strike, aimed shot, quick shot) must be learned first Watch the colored area under the animal while it winds up — run out of it before the attack lands to dodge Animals you hit will turn and fight; some herbivores run away instead (see Wild animals) · if it can reach you it always strikes back, even when you stand in the safe zone around a Harbor or have lured it far from home — see When an animal is hit

Numbers are the move's damage multiplier (1.0 = normal hit) · several numbers = several strikes Weapon   Normal hit   Special moves (multiplier) Bare Handed (attack 40)   1.0   Kick 0.8 · heavy hit 1.3 · punch combo 0.6 ×3 One-Handed (axe · knife/sword · hammer)   1.0   Heavy hit 2.2 · flurry 0.9 / 1.1 / 1.33 · stab 2.8 Two-Handed   1.0   Heavy hit 2.2 · sweep 1.1 / 1.6 · strike 2.5 Spear   1.0   Heavy thrust 2.2 · dash thrust 1.1 ×3 Bow / Crossbow   1.0   Quick shot 1.0 / 1.0 / 1.22 · aimed shot 2.1 [!note] Holding a weapon uses the weapon's attack (the bare-hand 40 is not added), then your character's attack bonus is added · axes, swords and hammers share the same move multipliers; they differ in their mastery skills

Damage = attack × move multiplier × penetration multiplier × direction multiplier × critical Attack = the attack of the weapon in your hand (bare hands 40) + your character's attack bonus (tags, built-in gear bonuses, food, titles, house ambiance) — the same number as on the character screen (Character stats) Penetration multiplier = 2.2 to the power of ((your armor penetration − animal defense) ÷ 100) · your armor penetration = the weapon's (bare hands 40) + your character's penetration bonus Difference 0 = ×1 · penetration ahead by 100 or more = ×2.2 (cap) · defense ahead by 100 or more = ×0.45 (floor) Animal defense grows with level (usually level × 5, e.g. Raptor Lv10 = 50) and is multiplied by the island's Unstable Index Hit chance = 50% + move accuracy × 45% (normal moves = 95%) · heavy moves −4% · + 0.1% per point of your character's Accuracy above 100 · always between 35% and 99% Critical hit chance 10% (heavy moves 18%) + 1% per Critical point (max 95%) · damage ×1.9 Examples (hit from the front, no critical · no character bonuses) Weapon   Move   Target   Damage per hit Bare Handed   Normal   Compsognathus Lv1   42 Bare Handed   Normal   Raptor Lv10   30 Stone Axe Lv15   Normal   Raptor Lv10   95 Stone Axe Lv15   Heavy hit   Raptor Lv10   209 Bone Knife Lv15   Stab   Sabertooth Lv40   94 Bone Bow Lv30   Normal shot   Raptor Lv10   163 Attack bonuses really count: a Lv30 two-handed stone axe (attack 154 · penetration 134) normal hit on a Lv30 Raptor (from the side) =

Some skill lines give moves a chance for that hit to ignore the animal's defense completely (counted as if the animal had 0 defense — direction, critical and body parts still apply as normal) · skills covering the same move add up Skill   Moves affected   Per level (3 levels) Backstab (penetration line)   One-handed stab   +10% Sword specialization   One-/two-handed normal and special moves   +6% Spear specialization   All spear moves   +6% Bow specialization   All bow moves   +10%

Every hit adds "blow power" to the animal's gauge. When the gauge reaches the species' stagger resistance, the animal staggers and the attack it is winding up is cancelled, then the gauge starts over · if it isn't hit for 4 seconds, the gauge resets Blow power per hit   Value Bow · bare hand · one-handed · crossbow (normal hit)   60 · 80 · 90 · 100 Two-handed (normal hit) · heavy hit · stab   120 · 150 · 180 Two-handed strike / second sweep swing   240 Animal   Resistance   One-handed normal hits needed Compsognathus · Phenacodus   140   2 Raptor   420   5 Sabertooth · Direwolf   560   7 Mammoth   1,120   13 Tyrannosaurus   1,575   18

Every move has its own hit area (circle · cone · rectangle) and the server checks each hit against it Area moves (flurry · sweep · stab · strike · punch combo) can hit several animals at once, up to 6 per swing · only animals on the island you're standing on · on a Lawless Island they hit enemy players too (6 targets in total) Animal attacks are cones/rectangles taken from their real moves (e.g. a raptor's tail swipe hits behind it) · the yellow/red area on screen = where the hit really lands

Direction: most animals take ×0.8 from the front · ×1.0 from the sides · ×1.2 from behind (Tyrannosaurus is reversed: front ×1.2 · back ×0.8) · you also take ×1.2 when an animal hits you from behind Body parts: each hit lands on the head/body/legs/tail at random depending on the direction. Each part has its own health; when it breaks: Broken legs → the animal walks/runs at 60% speed and is easier to hit Broken head or tail → the animal hits weaker or misses more often Broken parts heal by themselves after 10 minutes · when butchering, items from broken parts come out halved (except meat) Axe mastery skills add +6% body-part damage per level

Some green tags on weapons/gear make animals bleed (health drains over time — if it dies you get a normal carcass) or make animals that hit you miss more often · bleeding does not stagger or stun · see Tags for the tag list

Animals use the same formula: animal attack × 2.2 to the power of ((animal penetration − your defense) ÷ 100) · your defense = the defense of every armor piece + defense bonuses from skills/tags/gear/food/titles (the same value as on the character screen) · armor reduces damage but never blocks it completely; high-level animals hit very hard Animal   Your defense   Damage taken Raptor Lv10   0   35 Raptor Lv10   50   24 Sabertooth Lv40   100   176 Mammoth Lv50   150   466 Tyrannosaurus Lv60   300   952 After the damage is worked out there is still a chance to auto-dodge (no damage at all) and to auto-block (less damage) — dodge is rolled first, block only if you didn't dodge

sec.h: How much defense and blocking help
sec.x: A Lv30 character wearing armor with 122.5 total defense, holding a Lv30 two-handed stone axe (attack 154) · damage per hit (from the side, no critical) Animal   Armor only   + all Defense skills (+100 → 222.5)   Armor + block   All skills + block Raptor Lv30   54   25   8   1 Sabertooth Lv40   176   92   130   46 Mammoth Lv50   466   391   420   345 A block removes weapon attack × 0.3 = 154 × 0.3 ≈ 46 per blocked hit · at least 1 damage remains All Defense skills + all max-Health skills (Health 472 → 722): a Lv30 Raptor needs 9 → 29 hits to kill you · a Lv40 Sabertooth 3 → 8 · a Lv50 Mammoth still 2 [!warn] Animals Lv40 and above can kill a lightly armored player in 1–3 hits — go as a team, use heavy moves to stagger, and dodge the colored areas in time

Every time an animal lands a hit, you have an auto-dodge chance = Evasion × 0.1% (max 15%) — on a dodge you see «Dodged», lose no health, and the Defense category gets the same exp as dodging with a roll Evasion   Dodge chance 0 (default)   0% 30   3% 150 or more   15% (cap) Evasion comes from some gear (e.g. the improved melee combat outfit), tags, titles or food — no skill level gives Evasion yet Works with every weapon, bare hands included

Hold a melee weapon (sword/knife · axe · blunt weapon · spear) that still has Durability, and when an animal hits you (and you didn't auto-dodge) you have a chance to block and take less damage — no button, nothing to press Block chance = 5% + 0.25% × Defense category level (max 20% — exactly at category Lv60) Damage removed = the attack of the weapon you hold × 0.3 (your character's attack bonus is not included) · at least 1 damage remains On screen it shows as the reduced damage number like a normal hit (no «blocked» text) The blocked part wears your weapon by half of the amount blocked (like when you hit) · armor only wears from the remaining damage A blocked hit gives Defense exp equal to a roll dodge, instead of the exp for taking a hit Bare hands, bows, crossbows = can't block · blocking doesn't stagger the animal or counter-attack Defense category level   Block chance 1   5.25% 30   12.5% 60   20%
Hitting an animal repeatedly drains its stun gauge until it freezes (stunned) or collapses with stars over its head. It can't attack during that time and can be captured — see Taming

You can hit players only on the Lawless Islands (open from level 56) — on every other island your only enemies are animals Same moves and formula as against animals, but damage against players is multiplied by ×0.8 (melee, area moves included) / ×0.35 (bow, crossbow) · the target can still roll, auto-dodge and auto-block as usual Party members, clanmates and allied clans can't hit each other · players are never stunned by players · no exp for hitting players Everything else (arrival shield · what drops when you die) is on Lawless Islands (PvP)

The accuracy value on weapons themselves and the animals' evasion are not used for hit chance yet (hit chance comes from the move + your character's Accuracy) · knockback moves have no push effect · there is no manual guard move (only auto-block)

d: Five level 60 islands where players can fight each other — open from Lv56 · who can hit whom · damage · the arrival shield · what you drop when you die

sec.x: On normal islands players can't hurt each other — your only enemies are animals. The exception is the five Lawless Islands (the client calls this area the "Savage Islands"), where players from different sides can fight. Whoever dies leaves loot for others to pick up. No law, no land claims — just high-level resources and the toughest animals in the game.

Sail to a Lawless Island once you reach level 56 Attack players who aren't in your party, clan or allied clan — area moves can hit several enemies at once Pick up the packages other players drop when they die Gather and hunt on a level 60 island (animals Lv88–99)

d: Animal temperaments, counterattacks, island-based levels, herds and alphas, predators hunting prey, movement/sleep, and what you get from butchering

sec.x: Every island is home to herds of dinosaurs and prehistoric animals. Some attack the moment they see you, some run, some ignore you until they are hit. Animals have levels based on their island, sleep at night, hunt each other in front of you, and leave a carcass you can butcher for meat, leather and bones. Raptor Tyrannosaurus Sabertooth Mammoth

Hunt animals and butcher their carcasses into materials (see Combat) Capture animals to raise as pets (see Taming) Challenge the alpha of each island Watch predators hunt prey · sneak past animals sleeping at night

Temperament   Behavior Aggressive   Sees you within 8 tiles (closer if you have Stealth) → notices you in 2.5 seconds (alphas 1.5) → roars and chases · gives up once more than 32 tiles from home Neutral   Ignores you until hit, then fights back Skittish   Runs away when hit or when a predator comes After 20 seconds out of combat, animals regenerate 0.3% health per second · Tyrannosaurus and Apatosaurus regenerate 1% per second · Allosaurus does not regenerate Giving up the chase far from home doesn't mean you can hit it for free — an animal you're hitting will always strike back if it can reach you, see When an animal is hit [!tip] If you hit an animal and then leave it alone for a long time, it heals back — keep the pressure on when hunting big animals

Aggressive and neutral animals that get hit turn on whoever hit them — standing in a safe zone or luring them far from home won't let you hit them for free If it can reach you, it strikes back: if you've hit it within the last 20 seconds and you're inside its counter range (the reach of that species' longest attack + 1 tile), it hits back every time — even when lured more than 32 tiles from home, or when you're standing in a safe zone Far from home: more than 32 tiles from home it won't keep chasing — step out of its counter range and it gives up (you still can't lure it any farther) Safe zones (12-tile radius around Harbors and arrival points): animals never step inside — hit one from inside the zone and it runs up to the edge and strikes back if it can reach you If you stand deeper inside where it can't reach you, it roars a warning once and just watches (it doesn't swing attacks that can't land) After 10 seconds of not being able to reach you, it loses interest, walks back home and its health refills to full Idle, wandering animals avoid walking into safe zones · any already inside slowly walk out on their own Aggressive animals that spotted you and gave chase on their own (you haven't hit them) still give up when you enter a safe zone Skittish animals still run away when hit, as in the original game (no counterattack) · stunned/collapsed animals don't attack [!warn] A safe zone stops animals from running in after you, but it doesn't protect you from counterattacks — if yo

On an Unstable Island the health and attack of every animal (alphas included) are multiplied by 1 + (Unstable Index − 1) × 0.25 · the level shown over its head does not change Unstable Index   1   3   4   7   10 Multiplier   ×1   ×1.5   ×1.75   ×2.5   ×3.25

Public islands hold 6–12 animals per 64×64-tile area depending on terrain (see below), living in herds of up to 6 animals, using the species from that island's table Every island keeps at least 3 herds with ≥ 3 animals each — if hunting drops it below that, the missing herd returns to its spot after 3 minutes (aggressive) · 2 minutes (skittish) · 4 minutes (neutral) Safehouses, tutorial islands and peaceful islands are not topped up Areas with nobody around for 30 minutes put their herds to rest and set them up again when someone returns

How many animals live in each 64×64-tile area depends on the island's terrain: Terrain   Animals per area   Split into herds Grassland · savanna · tropical forest · temperate forest   12   2 herds × 6 Swamp · tundra · other terrain   9   a herd of 6 + a herd of 3 Snow islands · desert · volcanic   6   1 herd × 6 Areas that already hold more than this are not culled — they thin out naturally as animals are hunted or migrate The 3-herd minimum per island and the alphas are unchanged

A herd settling somewhere new (a herd moving in, or one added when an area opens) picks a random spot on land in the area at least 4 tiles from water and more than 8 tiles from any herd of the same species — herds no longer pile up on the shore or at the edge of the area If more than 6 animals of the same species are within 8 tiles of each other, the extras get split off: A predator nearby (within 16 tiles) → the closest one hunts the extras right away, without waiting to get hungry · the ones it kills are reborn in another herd of that species that isn't full, or at a new home (not back in the same pile) No predator → the extras move off to a new home on their own Alphas, elite leaders, fixed-spot animals, storage/rift guards and players' pets don't count · moves stay inside the same 64×64-tile area

Wild herds don't stay put forever — in areas where players are present: Herds that are still whole move away from time to time (about 10–30 minutes, random per herd · one herd per area at a time) — they walk away from people toward the edge and vanish once they are at least 23 tiles from every player, then a new herd settles at a random spot in the area (appearing out of sight and walking in), which may be a species you've never seen there A herd that fails to leave (someone keeps following it or fighting it for too long) gives up and returns to its old home A herd that is wiped out is not replaced by a new herd — its members are reborn into the same herd one by one, see Population recovery · the exception is a herd wiped out while it was leaving: a new herd moves in after about 20 minutes Sleeping herds can migrate without walking (they vanish when nobody is nearby) Areas with nobody around don't rotate · returning to an area you left for a long time rotates it once when you get back Areas never hold more animals than the numbers by terrain Never migrate: alphas/elite leaders · fixed-spot animals · animals guarding storages or rifts · animals that are fighting, chasing, being hunted, dazed or eating a carcass · no migration on Tamed Islands, safehouses or peaceful islands

Most islands have one alpha per alpha species (e.g. the Alpha Tyrannosaurus). Alphas are always aggressive and never sleep Topic   Value Health   ×2.5 of the same species (at least 2,000 + 50 × level) Elite leaders   ×1.5 (at least 250 + 12 × level) Respawn at the same spot   30 minutes (elite leaders 10 minutes) EXP for the kill   ×4 of a normal animal of the same level (elite leaders ×1.8) Examples   Alpha Tyrannosaurus Lv60 ≈ 389,191 · Allosaurus Lv60 ≈ 96,914 · Elephantulus Lv60 = 5,000 Alphas and elite leaders are island level ±5 like every other animal (Animal levels) · on islands of level 55 and up they roll in the island's range (island 55 → 60–70 · island 60 → 88–99 — Islands of level 55 and up) · so the Lv60 examples above show up on level-55 islands No alphas on Tamed Islands or safehouses · on Unstable Islands their health is multiplied by the Index as well

In areas where players are present, hungry aggressive carnivores actually chase down other animals in front of you They only hunt neutral/skittish animals of a different species and no higher level · alphas neither hunt nor get hunted · players' pets are never hunted Skittish prey runs once the predator is within 8 tiles · neutral prey fights back After a kill the predator eats for 20 seconds, then rests from hunting for 10 minutes · it gives up a chase after 60 seconds The kill leaves a carcass you can butcher, but with half the meat (leather/bones are complete) · no EXP/quest credit since you didn't kill it Hit a predator mid-hunt and it turns on you · a predator already chasing you won't switch to hunting animals At most 2 hunts at a time per area · for when predators go hunting see Hunting when hungry · no hunting on peaceful islands

Each predator gets hungry every ~15 minutes on average (random 7.5–22.5 minutes per animal) and goes after nearby prey within 16 tiles A predator needs about 8 bites to kill its prey · big prey fights back harder, and the predator can lose Anything that dies in a hunt (prey or predator) is reborn into its herd one at a time, the same as any other death — see Population recovery · the carcass can still be butchered (half the meat) Still at most 2 hunts at a time per area · predators rest 10 minutes after eating · sleeping predators and those chasing a player don't hunt

Running: animals use their real run animation when chasing or fleeing (same speed as before, 0.925 tiles/second · walking 0.575) Sleeping: a game day lasts 48 minutes: dawn (4:30–8) · day (8–17) · dusk (17–21) · night (21–4:30) Night animals (wolves, sabertooths, etc.) are awake at dusk and night · everything else is awake except at night Outside its waking hours each animal has a 45% chance to be asleep (re-rolled daily) · sleeping animals don't wander, chase or hunt They wake if you come within 4 tiles (3 tiles with Stealth) or hit them, then stay awake for 2 minutes · alphas and water animals never sleep Flinching: every hit plays a short flinch (visual only) · only a critical hit or a full stagger gauge interrupts the attack an animal is winding up Roaring: aggressive animals roar the first time they spot you (standing still ≤ 2 seconds) before chasing · alphas roar when a fight starts · once per 60 seconds per animal · no damage · some species have no roar (Sabertooth, Mammoth, Allosaurus, etc.) Stunned/collapsed: see Taming [!tip] Gathering at night on islands with aggressive (non-nocturnal) animals is safer — just don't walk right next to a sleeping one

A dead animal leaves a carcass for 15 minutes (each butchering resets the timer) Tap the carcass → choose a part to butcher, one piece at a time until it's empty · parts you haven't unlocked with butchering skills are greyed out Item level = animal level + your Butchering skill bonus, but never above your character level Animal   Carcass drops (amount per carcass) Compsognathus   Meat 1–2 · Carnivore Leg Bone 1–2 Raptor   Meat 2–3 · Carnivore Leg Bone 1–2 · Leather 1–2 · Teeth 1 Triceratops   Meat 5–8 · Herbivore Leg Bone/Rib 2–3 · Skull 1 · Horn 1–2 · Leather 2–3 Mammoth   Meat 7–10 · Herbivore Leg Bone/Rib 2–3 · Skull 1 · Ivory 1–2 · Pelt 2–3 · Fat 1–2 Tyrannosaurus   Meat 8–12 · Carnivore Leg Bone/Rib 3–4 · Large Skull 1 · Leather 3–4 · Teeth 1 Parts that were broken when the animal died give half (meat excluded) · carcasses left by predators give half the meat

Herd animals that die — killed by a player, eaten by a predator, captured or caught in a trap — don't pop back right away; they are reborn into the same herd one at a time: Wait = about 3.3 minutes × the number of animals the herd is missing (20 minutes ÷ 6) — missing 1 waits 3.3 minutes · missing 2 waits 6.7 minutes · … · a whole herd of 6 wiped out waits 20 minutes before the first one returns After each birth the timer restarts based on how many are still missing · more deaths while waiting restart it too — so small remnants come back slowly, and a wiped-out herd of 6 takes about 70 minutes to fill up again If players are nearby, the newcomer appears out of sight (at least 23 tiles from every player, on the herd's side) and walks into the herd · with nobody around it appears right in the herd Alphas/elite leaders respawn on their own timers (Alphas) · the 3-herds-per-island minimum always applies

d: Beat an animal below 30% health or stun it, then capture it with a Taming Herb — tame it in a pen before forming a bond

sec.x: Almost every wild animal can become your companion. The steps are weaken it → capture it with a Taming Herb → get its Rein → tame it in a pen → form a bond, and you get a pet that travels with you, can be ridden, helps in fights and produces goods. Capturing an animal and putting it in a pen

Capture a wild animal at ≤ 30% health or while it is stunned/collapsed (any health) Use blunt weapons or heavy moves to stun animals faster Tame captured animals in a taming pen, then bond with them as pets

Item   Level   Used for Novice Taming Herb   1–19   Capture tool — must be in your bag Standard Taming Herb   20–39   〃 Advanced Taming Herb   40–60   〃 Makeshift Taming Pen / Small Taming Pen   —   Taming the animals you capture The capture tool loses 3 durability per capture attempt (success or not) · pressing capture before the animal qualifies does not wear the tool

Hit the animal until it has ≤ 30% health or until it is stunned/collapsed (see the stun gauge below) Target it and press Capture  — the button is always pressable when you have a tool; the server checks the conditions Stand still for the 3-second bar (moving cancels) Success → the animal leaves the world and its Rein goes into your bag · failure → a message shows the chance that was rolled; try again after the 5-second cooldown If it doesn't qualify yet, a server message (in Thai) tells you to get its health below 30% or stun it first Carcasses and rift guardians can't be captured · you must stand close · some species can't be captured at all (button locked) [!tip] If you walk away from a low-health animal it can heal back above 30% (it regenerates 20 seconds after combat) — capture quickly

sec.h: When your animal slots are full

Every 10 points of Capture Ability (on the stats window) count as 1 extra character level when the capture chance is worked out Comes from   Amount Capture skills (Capturing Bipedal/Quadrupedal Dinos · Capturing Mammals, etc. — 10 steps)   +4 to +7 per step (55 in total) Clan Research Ecology   +5 Example: a level 20 character capturing an animal at 30% health Animal   No Capture Ability   15   35   55 (all skills) Lv20   74%   82%   87%   90% Lv25   17%   40%   63%   77% Lv30   2%   2%   2%   25% [!note] The in-game hint says the capture tool's level matters, but on this server the chance uses your character level (plus Capture Ability) against the animal's level

Every animal has a stun gauge (for small animals it is roughly 2× their health · multiplied by the island's Unstable Index). Each hit drains it, and the animal moves through these stages Stage   Gauge left   Effect   In-game message Weakened   ≤ ⅓   Warning message only   "… is losing strength." Stunned   ≤ ⅑   Frozen: no attacks, no walking, no fleeing · the attack it was winding up is cancelled   "… is stunned." Collapsed   0   Falls down with stars over its head   "… collapsed!" Recovered   time runs out   Gauge full again   "… steadied itself." A heavy hit can skip from weakened straight to collapsed · you can capture at any moment while it's stunned/collapsed When the fight ends (the animal gives up or returns home) the gauge silently refills · the gauge does not recover by itself mid-fight Animal   Stunned for (seconds)   Collapsed for (seconds) Compsognathus · Phenacodus   6   6 Raptor · Direwolf   8   8 Sabertooth   10   10 Iguanodon   12   12 Triceratops · Mammoth   4   6 Tyrannosaurus   5   3

sec.h: After the capture: taming in a pen
sec.x: Taming pen Build/place a taming pen and put the Rein into it Start taming — it takes 60 seconds · base success chance 60% (maximum 100%) Feed it during taming to help: Food   Effect All-Purpose Taming Feed   Chance +10% · time −30% Fast Taming Feed   Time −50% Meat / Minnow   Time −10 seconds per piece When time is up, collect the result: success → the animal is tamed and gets a random rank (S · A · B · C · D, whichever that species can have) · failure → the animal escapes to the wild and the Rein is lost Use the tamed animal's Rein to form a bond → it becomes your pet (the Rein's level must not exceed your Survival category level) — continue at Pets Taming time can't be cut below half [!note] Animal traps give carcass items (meat, leather, bones), not live animals to raise

Wild animals of Lv61–99 (on islands of level 55 and up — Wild animals) can be captured as usual · the Rein you get shows the animal's real level (up to 99) The bonding rule is unchanged: your Survival category level must reach the Rein's level — Survival tops out at 60, so you can't form a bond with Lv61+ animals yet If your category is too low, the game won't let you form the bond and the server also refuses with a message (in Thai) saying the animal's level is above your Survival level · the Rein stays in your bag Lv61–70 pets you already bonded earlier are kept and can still level up to 99 (Pets) [!warn] Breaking the bond of a pet above level 60 gives you a Rein at its real level, which can't be bonded again — don't break the bond of pets above level 60

d: Summon pets to fight, ride and carry items, feed them, use their active skills, produce milk in pens, revive them and keep them from aging

sec.x: Animals you capture and tame become your pets once you form a bond. Summon them to follow you, ride them, carry items in their bag, let them help in fights with their active skill, or put them in a pen to produce milk or train for levels. A bonded pet

Summon / return — one at a time · animals in a pen, roaming, or knocked out can't be summoned Ride — rideable species only (speed depends on species, e.g. Raptor 700 · Mammoth 160) Animal bag — slots depend on species, e.g. Raptor 10 · Sabertooth 30 · Ankylosaurus 150 · Triceratops 240 · Mammoth 300 · Brachiosaurus 500 Feed to restore vigor · rename (1–16 characters) · set free (the animal is gone forever · items in its bag go back to your bag) Roaming — let up to 5 animals roam your Tamed Island (they don't age, can't produce or train · items in their bag disappear) Redraw rank (species with several ranks) — you see the rolled rank first, then accept it or keep the old one

sec.h: How many animals you can own
sec.x: Skill   Maximum owned animals None   8 Animal Handling I / II / III / IV   10 / 12 / 14 / 16 The pet window and the top bar show «count / maximum» Counted: summoned animals, stored animals, animals in a pen · not counted: animals roaming your Tamed Island, and Reins you have not bonded yet Once full you can't capture wild animals, bond Reins or bring a roaming animal back — a message tells you, tools don't wear and the Reins stay in your bag · set one roaming or set one free first Swapping one for one (send 1 roaming, bring 1 back) always works, even when full If you already own more than the limit, none of your animals disappear — you just can't add more until you are below the limit The pet window's button for bringing a roaming animal back now works

Reins from animal packages (once sold in the Shop) hold an already tamed animal — press Form a Bond from your bag right away, no pen needed · its rank is rolled the same way as a successful pen taming · full health and fullness · it still counts toward how many animals you can own

A pet's vigor (300 max for every species) drops only while it is summoned, and is used for fighting, skills and production Species   Vigor lost per second   Full to empty Raptor · Direwolf · Oviraptor · Ornithomimus, etc. (18 species)   0.05   ~100 minutes All other species (83)   0.09   ~55 minutes Food   Vigor restored Leaf · Minnow   40 Meat   50 Nutritious Animal Feed   500 Highly Nutritious Animal Feed   700 Infinite Vigor Feed   Vigor stops dropping for a while Only animal food can be fed (the feeding menu lists it) · a full pet can't eat normal food Attack and Provoke skills need at least half of max vigor (150)

A pet lives for 30 days from bonding, then shows as "Old" — its stats are halved (health, health regen, attack, defense, speed, bag, max vigor, accuracy, etc.) Roaming on your Tamed Island stops the aging clock Animal Anti-Aging Remedy (15/30/45/60 days) gives life time back, but never beyond the full lifespan

A pet and a pen Put a pet in an animal pen (Makeshift Pen · Small Pen · Medium Pen) → choose the pet → Production or Training → wait for the timer, then collect items and pet EXP Production   Time   Vigor used   Pet EXP   Unlocks at pet level Production Lv.1   1 h   150   40   1 Production Lv.2   2 h   170   110   10 Production Lv.3   4 h   190   290   20 Production Lv.4   8 h   270   1,100   30 Production Lv.5   10 h   460   3,900   40 Production Lv.6   12 h   590   15,000   50 Milk comes from production by mammal pets such as Phenacodus, Macrauchenia, Female Megaloceros, Direwolf, Skunkodus: each round gives Milk or Animal Droppings, 50% each Male Megaloceros only gives Animal Droppings · Bumblebee Phenacodus gives Honey 50% / Milk 30% / Animal Droppings 20% Amount per round = (2 + pet level ÷ 10) × the production level's multiplier (1 · 5/3 · 7/3 · 10/3 · 14/3 · 6), rounded down — a Lv1 pet on Production Lv.1 gives 2 9–17% chance of a bonus item (coin · worm · corn seed) · item level = pet level Training Lv.1 takes 1 h and 150 vigor for 100 pet EXP (no items) Production Lv.5–6 needs more than 300 vigor, so raise your pet's max vigor first [!tip] You can feed pets inside the pen (feed button on the pen screen) — top up vigor before starting a new production round

Pets can level up to 99 (the original game stopped at 60) with pet EXP, e.g. from production and training in pens Pets that were stuck at an old cap level up again the next time they gain EXP, counting the EXP they had stored up You can form a bond when your Survival category level reaches the Rein's level · Reins show the animal's real level, but Survival tops out at 60 — so newly captured wild animals of Lv61+ can't be bonded yet (Animals above level 60) · pets above 60 come from levelling your pets up, or ones you bonded earlier

d: The 8 basic abilities, max Health/Energy, combat stats, crafting/gathering stats, resistances and power ratings — where they come from, how they're calculated, which ones really matter

sec.x: The character info screen shows many values — the numbers it shows are now the same values the server really uses, counting every source (skills · titles · gear and tags · food · house ambiance · buffs and status effects such as personal/clan research, buffs from pets, event buffs). This page explains where each one comes from, how it's calculated and what it does on this server. When a buff or house ambiance runs out, your stats go back right away · negative statuses (e.g. the death penalty) really lower your stats too Value   Comes from   Affects 8 basic abilities   Character level + skill category levels + title + food/gear   Endurance → max Health · Will → max Energy Max Health / Energy · regen per second   Base + level + basic abilities + bonuses from every source   The on-screen gauges (Survival) Combat stats   The weapon and gear you wear + character bonuses · skill effects on moves   Damage dealt and taken · auto-dodge/auto-block (Combat) Crafting / gathering stats   Character level + learned skills + bonuses from every source   Mastery ladder · craft/gather success chance (Crafting · Gathering) Climate resistance   Time spent on islands of each climate + gear   Entry gates for high-Index islands · less weather fatigue (Weather) 3 power ratings   Weighted from the values above   Display only

Ability = 10 + 0.5 × (character level − 1) + 0.35 × sum of (feeding category level − 1) + title bonus + food/gear/tag bonus · the part from level and skill categories is at least 1 and at most 100 · bonuses from titles, food, gear and buffs are added on top and can take it above 100 · the character screen rounds to whole numbers Ability   Fed by skill categories Strength   Melee · Construction Endurance   Defense · Survival Agility   Melee · Ranged Dexterity   Weapon/Tool · Tailoring · Processing Perception   Gathering · Ranged Intelligence   Cooking · Processing Will   Survival · Butchering Charisma   Cooking · Tailoring Example: a Lv30 character with Survival Lv20 and Defense Lv10 → Endurance = 10 + 14.5 + 0.35 × (19 + 9) = 34.3 [!note] The basic abilities that actually do something are Endurance (max Health) and Will (max Energy) — Endurance/Will from food, tags and gear raise the gauges too · the other 6 are shown on the character screen but aren't used in any damage or chance calculation yet
