d: Character level, skill categories, skill points, Skill Rewind, the career you pick at character creation, and the Career Guide

sec.x: Your character grows in two ways. Character level goes up from everything you do. Skill categories are separate tracks, and each one only grows from its own kind of work. Character levels give you Skill Points to learn skills. A skill category's level decides which skill ranks you are allowed to learn. Career Guide card for the melee line

Gather, craft, build, hunt and tame to earn character EXP and skill category EXP Spend Skill Points on new skills. Skills give crafting recipes, combat actions and stat bonuses Use Skill Rewind to get points back and learn a different line Pick a career when you create your character. It starts one category at Lv.20 and gives starting items Finish courses in the Career Guide for item rewards and a title

The maximum character level is 99 — see Max level 99 Doing things at your own level takes about 40 actions (weight 1) per level, at any level EXP also depends on the level of what you do. Lower-level work gives less; higher-level work gives a little more A great success gives ×1.5 Killing an alpha gives ×4 EXP · an elite leader ×1.8 (Wild animals) · kills made with fast multi-hit moves still get their full kill EXP Unattended crafting at a workbench gives character and category EXP when you collect the finished item (not when you start) · cancelling refunds the materials but gives no EXP · the EXP goes to whoever started the job, even if someone else takes the item out Eating, drinking, washing and resting give no EXP Action   Weight (higher = more EXP) Gathering · planting and harvesting   1 Crafting · butchering · dodging an attack · discovering a new spot   2 Building · hunting · capturing/taming   3 The level multiplier is (10 + 2 × level of the thing) ÷ (10 + 2 × your level), at least ×0.1 and at most ×1.5. Example: a Lv.30 character gathering a Lv.10 resource gets about ×0.43. Every character level-up gives Skill Points (+5 to +35 depending on the level range), +4 max health and +1.5 max energy. Levels 2, 5 and 10 also give a level title.

The maximum character level is 99 (the original game stopped at 60) EXP needed up to Lv80 follows the original game's table · Lv81–99 extend the same curve, getting steeper · doing things at your own level still takes about 40 actions per level at every level If you were stuck at an old cap (60 or 70), your next EXP gain takes you up one level right away, then you keep levelling one level at a time — no stored-up EXP makes you skip several levels at once Max health +4 and max energy +1.5 per level stay the same all the way to 99 · Skill Points per level go up after Lv70 — see Skill Points (1,200 at Lv99) Skill categories still stop at Lv60 — levels 61–99 unlock no new skill ranks, but the extra Skill Points let you learn other skills you haven't finished Level-up   EXP needed from the previous level   Total EXP from the start 60 → 61   489,728   4,022,264 64 → 65   801,941   6,715,414 69 → 70   1,469,595   12,572,235 74 → 75   2,665,177   23,231,733 79 → 80   4,789,771   42,448,356 84 → 85   8,511,464   76,746,238 89 → 90   14,944,434   137,214,551 94 → 95   25,936,370   242,593,536 98 → 99   39,976,765   379,623,456

Some worn items have an Acquired EXP stat, and some status effects raise EXP too — character EXP from actions × (1 + sum of EXP bonuses from your active statuses) × (1 + the bonus from worn items) · the total multiplier stays between ×0.1 and ×10 Source   Extra EXP Somebody's Apple (accessory)   +200% Prodigal Pioneer status (returning players)   +100% EXP event status   +20% / +50% / +100% depending on the event Delicious status   +3% e.g. Apple → ×3 · Apple + Delicious → ×3.09 · Prodigal Pioneer + Delicious → ×2.03 The EXP number that pops up shows the extra part in brackets, e.g. «206 (+103)» It does not multiply skill category EXP or quest/mission reward EXP

There are 12 categories you can train. Each goes from Lv.1 to 60 and cannot go above your character level. Once a category catches up with your character level, its EXP bar stays full — when your character levels up (or you log in again), every category with a stuck full bar goes up 1 level by itself right away, no need to wait for more EXP · levels that need Research still need you to start the research as before The Melee category level boosts melee moves · the Ranged category boosts bow/crossbow moves (each move uses its own category) · combat bonuses from categories update as soon as the category levels up Category   Earns EXP from Survival   Capturing/taming animals · discovering new spots or new animal species Melee   Hunting with melee weapons Ranged   Hunting with ranged weapons Defense   Dodging attacks · taking hits Butchering   Butchering carcasses Gathering   Gathering plants, wood, stone and ore (Gathering) Cooking · Weapon/Tool · Tailoring · Processing   Crafting recipes of that category (Crafting) Construction   Building structures (Building) Farming   Planting seeds · harvesting (Farming)

Category EXP per action depends on the level of what you do compared with the category level: Level of the thing vs. category level   Category EXP per action Same or higher   3 1–5 levels lower   2 6–15 levels lower   1 More than 15 levels lower   0 A great success gives ×1.5, but never more than 3 per action Hitting an animal gives EXP in proportion to damage dealt compared with the animal's health Spamming one category far more than normal within one hour slowly lowers the EXP, but never to zero Category level   EXP needed for the next level 1–3   1 10   3 20   7 30   14 40   27 50   51 59   90

Some category levels need Research before they can go up. When the EXP bar is full at one of these levels, start Research on the skill page and wait for the timer. Every category has research steps except Survival. Category level   Research time 20   5 minutes 25   20 minutes 30   1 hour 35   2 hours 40   4 hours 45   12 hours 50   24 hours 55   48 hours 59   72 hours You can research one category at a time Research can only start while the category level is below your character level While researching, keep doing that category's work to shorten the timer (EXP × category level ÷ 10 seconds per action), up to 25% of the total time

The Instant Completion button on a category under research costs T-Stones based on the time left — 10 T-Stones for every 30 minutes left (rounded up), at least 10 and at most 100 · the price on the button drops by itself as time passes and always matches what is charged Time left   Price Up to 30 minutes   10 T-Stones 30 minutes – 1 hour   20 1 – 2 hours   30–40 4 hours   80 Over 4.5 hours   100 (max) e.g. finishing right after starting research at Lv30 (1 hour) = 20 · Lv40 (4 hours) = 80 · Lv45 and up = 100 Starting research in a new category while another is still running = you pay the Instant Completion price of the running one · if the new category can't start yet, nothing is skipped and nothing is charged Not enough T-Stones = no skip (the message is in Thai) · the confirm box shows a gem icon, but the balance used is your T-Stones

With Academic Ambiance from a house (Buffs), research started while the buff is on takes −20% (e.g. 5 minutes → 4 minutes) · the Skill page shows the shortened time before you start · reductions add up to at most 90%

Learn: open the Skill page, choose a category and learn the next rank. Your character must be alive. Skill Rewind: removes one rank at a time, starting from the top rank, and refunds the points right away. A main skill cannot be removed while any of its sub-skills are still learned · free ranks (0 points) cannot be rewound, and trying doesn't use up your quota After a rewind your stats, Health/Energy bars, combat moves and blueprints update right away — no need to log out Rewind number that day   Cost 1–5   Free 6–15   1 Skill Rewind Voucher (if you have one · any kind works), otherwise 30 T-Stones Over 15   Not possible until the reset The quota resets every day at 22:00 Thai time (UTC+7), which is 15:00 UTC.

The Skill Reset Ticket clears all your skills at once — use it from your bag; the game asks you to confirm and shows your skill points before/after, then press Use Every rank that costs points is removed, including the skills your career gave you at the start, and all those points come back Free ranks (0 points) stay · skill category levels, your career and the daily Skill Rewind quota do not change One ticket is used per reset It cannot be used while a craft or a skill research is in progress — wait for it or cancel first Sold in the Shop for 5,000 T-Stones

The Career Guide button is on the skill page. It holds 58 courses, grouped by line and by difficulty 1–4. Each course is a list of skills to learn. d: Team up with other players, set up ranks, share land and storage, donate to the clan funds to level the clan up, and form alliances with other clans.

sec.x: Clan A clan is a permanent group of players. It has a leader, ranks, its own chat room, and shared Clan Enclaves and storage. The more members donate to the Clan Funds, the higher the clan level: more members, more alliance slots, and a buff that reduces what you drop when you die.

Create your own clan, or ask to join an existing one Set up ranks, name them, and choose what each rank may do Talk in the clan chat (works across all islands) Wear a clan honour flag on your back Declare a Clan Enclave and build/share storage there by rank Donate T-Stones to the Clan Funds → clan level goes up Form alliances with other clans Run clan research at a research center (paid from the Clan Funds)

Open the Clan menu → Create Clan → pick a name and pay the creation cost Or search for a clan and press Request to Join — wait for someone with the right to approve you (you can cancel your request) If someone invites you, a message appears on screen — go to that clan and request to join; you get in at once without approval Item   Value Creation cost   5,000 T-Stones Clan name   2–16 characters · must be unique Clans per character   1 at a time Clan notice / introduction   up to 300 / 500 characters Clan emblem image   up to 4 KB Leaving: if the leader leaves, leadership passes to the next-highest rank (same rank = whoever joined first). If the last member leaves, the clan is disbanded — all Clan Enclaves and the buildings on them go to that last leader. [!warn] When a clan is disbanded, the T-Stones in its Clan Funds are lost. They are not refunded.

d: Trade with other players at the Market for T-Stones (5% sales tax) and buy from the Shop with T-Stones — this server has a single currency and no real-money top-ups.

sec.x: T-Stone The main currency on this server is T-Stones. You use them to trade with other players at the Market, buy things in the Shop, pay for cargo, create a clan, and more. This server has no real-money top-ups — everything is bought with T-Stones earned in the game.

List items from your bag at the Market at any price you like Search/filter listings and buy what others are selling Star listings you like to keep them in Favorites Collect money from sales (minus a 5% tax) · take back items that didn't sell Buy from the Shop: the Skill Reset Ticket · animal/outfit/building packages · medicine · appearance change cards

Wallet This server uses a single wallet: T-Stones. Currency   Used for T-Stones   Main money — Market, Shop, cargo fees, clan creation, Clan Funds, etc. · you can hold up to 99,999,999 Loyalty   Separate points given as a bonus by some Shop items — spent in the Loyalty Shop Tickets   Some things are tickets (e.g. map-opening tickets), kept separately in your wallet Shop prices are shown with a Gem/Coin icon — on this server they cost the same number of T-Stones (1 to 1), and the balance shown under the Gem/Coin icons is your T-Stone balance. Where T-Stones come from: discovering new places on the map and full-exploration rewards · Quests · daily attendance · mini-games · Warp · gift mail (Mail) · selling at the Market

Open the Market menu → Sell tab Pick items from your bag (equipped, locked, or below 90% durability can't be listed — repair first) Set the price per item and how long to sell → confirm — the items leave your bag right away While on sale you can press Cancel Listing at any time; the item returns to your bag Set any price you like — there is no price cap You can pick several items at once; each is listed separately at the same price You sell the actual item — the buyer gets its durability, color and tags as they are Food on the Market does not spoil while listed (see Preserving)

Search by name, category, tag, price range and level range; sort by price, time, level or durability Many screens have a shortcut to search the Market, e.g. material slots when building/repairing Press Buy → pay T-Stones, the item goes straight into your bag · you can't buy your own listings Star listings to keep them in Favorites — the server remembers them after you log out

Listing is free — a 5% tax on the sale price is taken only once the item sells, when you collect the money (rounded up to a whole number). Open and read mail Receive attachments one mail at a time, or Receive All Delete mail you have already collected, or that has no attachments

d: Island types (Ancora, Safe House, Tamed Island, Unstable Islands, Civilized Islands, Lawless Islands) · Unstable Island lifespan · private Tamed Islands for Supporters · sailing, balloons, returning to a Stable Island · island levels, Unstable Index and danger

sec.x: The world of Durango is an archipelago. Every island has its own level and climate. Some islands are safe and permanent (you can settle there), others are Unstable Islands — more dangerous, with better loot, and only around for a limited time. Everyone on the server shares the same world: you meet, help and compete with other players on the same islands. An Unstable Island on the sailing map

Start on Ancora → build a raft → arrive at The Company's Safe House Take the Hot Air Balloon to claim your own Tamed Island, then declare a Domain · players with the Supporter role get a private Tamed Island and choose who may enter it Sail from a Harbor to Unstable Islands in 8 climates, level 15–60, to gather and hunt — an Unstable Island lasts 12 hours to 3 days, then disappears and a new one takes its place Pick your own difficulty with each island's Unstable Index (1–10) At level 56+, sail to the Lawless Islands where players can fight each other — Lawless Islands (PvP) Go home for free at any time with Sail to the last Stable Island or the warp buttons on Warps & Rifts

Type   Island level   Domain   Unstable Index   Island fatigue   Lifespan Ancora (starting island)   1   No   1 (stable)   None   Permanent The Company's Safe House   5   No   1 (stable)   None   Permanent Tamed Island   10   Yes (free expansion)   1 (stable)   None   Permanent Unstable Island   15–60   No   1–10   Yes   12 hours – 3 days Training island (tropical)   18   No   1 (stable)   Half   Permanent Civilized Island (abandoned city)   40   Yes   1 (stable)   Half   Permanent Event islands   20–60   No   1   Yes   12 hours – 3 days Lawless Island (PvP)   60 (enter from Lv56)   No   1   Yes   Permanent

Every new character starts on Ancora — the tutorial island, rebuilt from the original game's real map. Follow the tutorial, finish the raft (4 logs · 6 reed stems) and it carries you to the Safe House. Resources were rebuilt to match the original: everything is on ground you can walk to — nothing on cliffs or unreachable plateaus · the tutorial spots have what the tutorial asks for (dates at the train cars · reeds at the stream · stones by the lake · branches and stones at the bonfire · log trees and reeds around the small lake by the raft) — details in Getting Started Resource amounts and regrow speed are the same as on other islands (no special multiplier anymore) Resting at the bonfire on Ancora empties your fatigue in 5 seconds Animals: the Brachiosaurus stay in the lake only · 3 Compsognathus herds near the spawn valley and along the stream — harmless, they run when hit, a good first hunt (Compsognathus on Ancora and the Safe House) · the 2 at the train cars are scenery models You can sail back to visit Ancora from a Harbor, but you can only leave by raft — you must build it again every time

The hub for new players — K and the Company's staff, a workbench, a campfire, a notice board, a Harbor, a balloon station and Warp Holes you can use right away without finding them. If you haven't set a Waypoint anywhere, the Safe House is your "home". Harmless Compsognathus herds roam around the arrival point.

A level 10 grassland island for settling down — declare a Domain, build a house, farm, raise animals. Expanding a Domain on a Tamed Island is free, and there is no climate fatigue from the island itself. Tamed Islands have no wild animals at all — no dinosaurs or bosses spawn there, so it's a safe island for building and farming · your own pets and caged animals are unaffected · to hunt or tame, go to another island. Tamed Islands are a shared world — everyone who picks the same island layout lives on the same island. You see each other and can visit each other's homes, like a village where everyone stakes out their own plot. Spots already declared show as owned, so look for the next free one. (Supporters can use a private Tamed Island instead — see below.) Your first trip to your Tamed Island is by Hot Air Balloon from the Safe House (see Hot Air Balloon below). You can pick from 5 island layouts (next section).

The first time you press Leave at the balloon station, the Declare Tamed Island screen lets you pick from 5 grassland island layouts, each with a different map. Tamed Island layout 1 Tamed Island layout 2 Tamed Island layout 3 Tamed Island layout 4 Tamed Island layout 5 You choose once — the layout can't be changed afterwards Players who already have a Tamed Island keep it and are not moved Each layout is its own shared world — players who pick the same layout live together Same rules for all: level 10 · Index 1 · no wild animals · free Domain expansion

Players with the Supporter role get a private Tamed Island — the same layout you picked, but for that character only. Other players can't see it or enter it (except people you allow — next section). It's still the same server as everyone else: chat, friends, clans and the market work as usual. One per character · same island rules as the shared Tamed Island (level 10 · no wild animals · free Domain expansion) Switch by typing in chat: /tamed private = your private island (the default) · /tamed shared = the shared Tamed Island · typing it while on the Tamed Island moves you right away · anywhere else, it applies next time you go to your Tamed Island Everything you built on the shared Tamed Island stays where it is — the private island starts empty (you can move your old land over once — see "Moving your land to your private island") The role is checked every time you log in — if it ends, you go to the shared Tamed Island next time and your private island is kept; get the role back and you return Everyone else keeps using the shared Tamed Island as before

The island owner (a Supporter) decides who may enter in the Island Entry Permissions window (the Domain screen on the private island) — tick Clan Member · Friend · Outsider, several at once if you like ("Outsider" = everyone) Default = all closed, only the owner can enter Closing a group sends that group's visitors back to their own Tamed Island at once Up to 20 visitors at a time (the owner not counted) · allowed players can visit even while the owner is offline · an online owner gets a message when someone arrives Removing a visitor: tap them on your island → the kick-from-island button → they're sent back to their own Tamed Island · Block them = sent back at once and can't enter your island again To visit — use the sailing menu at a Harbor (Random Sailing) · you arrive at the island's arrival point On someone else's island: walk, chat and gather natural resources · inside the owner's land the owner's permissions apply (outsiders normally can't build or open boxes/cages) · you can't declare land or build outside the owner's land Only Supporters' private Tamed Islands can be visited this way (the shared Tamed Island is open to everyone anyway)

sec.h: Moving your land to your private island
sec.x: A Supporter can move their land from the shared Tamed Island to their private island once per character (no deadline) — houses, buildings, boxes with everything inside, cages and the animals in them are placed at the exact same spot on the private island. Type /tamed move in chat → you get a summary of what will move Type /tamed move confirm within 60 seconds to confirm (/tamed move cancel = cancel) Works while your private island has no land yet · if something on the private island is in the way, you're told to remove it first · a failed move, or no land on the shared island, costs nothing — your move stays available and everything stays put Things your friends built on your land move with it · other players' animals in your cages go back to their owners · anything outside your land stays where it is Confirming while standing on the shared Tamed Island takes you to your private island right away · afterwards the Tamed Island button takes you to the private island

Islands you reach by sailing — high-level resources and aggressive animals. Most islands of level 35 and above have Rifts and craters. The higher the level or Index, the more dangerous. You cannot declare Domains here · every one of them has a lifespan (next section). A level 18 tropical island with the survival tutorial (find a crater, find the harbor). You can sail there from any Harbor. Its Index is always 1, it has no predators, and island fatigue is halved.
Four abandoned cities at level 40 (grassland · temperate · tropical · tundra) — stable islands where you can declare a Domain. Island fatigue is halved.

Islands from the original game's past events (grassland festival · Summer Club · Season 1/2 islands) are open as normal islands with Index 1 and a lifespan like Unstable Islands. If you log out while on an event island, you'll wake up at home next time (see "Logging out on a temporary island" below).

Five level 60 islands (volcano · swamp · snowfield · temperate · tropical) where players can fight each other — open from level 56 · Index 1 · no lifespan · no Domains · details on Lawless Islands (PvP)

Walk to a Harbor and tap it → choose Sail The sea map opens — pick a climate/level, then an island by the Index you want Confirm "Do you want to move to the … island?" → you land at that island's arrival point Sailing is free — no T-Stones — and islands are not level-locked. You can go to a level 60 island at level 1, but you'll tire very fast · except the Lawless Islands, which need level 56+ Islands with Index 3 or higher need enough climate resistance (table below), or you can't set sail An island that is respawning (about 1.5 minutes after it expires) can't be sailed to Your pets and everything in your bag come with you

The Harbor's sailing menu has 2 buttons for visiting other players' private Tamed Islands (Visiting private Tamed Islands) To Tamed Island → search a player by name → pick who to visit Random Sailing → go to someone's island that is open to Outsiders and not full · none open = you get a message Sailing there is free · not allowed / full = you can't go, and a message says why

At the Harbor of an Unstable Island you get Sail to the last Stable Island and "Return to the Tamed Island harbor you started from?" — both take you straight to your home island, for free. Home island = the island where you used Designate as Waypoint (your own bed/tent) · never set = the Safe House Leaving any island clears that island's automatic checkpoint (a bed/tent Waypoint is kept)

Hot Air Balloon The balloon station at the Safe House offers two things: Leave — go to your Tamed Island (the first time, the Declare Tamed Island screen opens first so you can pick 1 of 5 layouts) Board Hot Air Balloon — fly freely over the island, even across water. Free to board · flights last up to 15 minutes, then you land automatically · you can't land on water/cliffs — you'll be sent back to the station

sec.h: Logging out on a temporary island
sec.x: If you log out or disconnect while on a temporary island — an Unstable Island with Index 2+, an event island, or the training island — the next time you log in you'll be on your home island (or the Safe House) with the message "The island disappeared and you were moved to your Waypoint." Everything you carry and your pets come with you. Stable islands (Safe House · Ancora · Tamed Island · Civilized Islands · Lawless Islands · Unstable Islands with Index 1) → you come back where you were Arriving on a temporary island by boat doesn't move you — it only happens on the next login after you log out An island that expires while you're offline → you're always moved to your Waypoint, even at Index 1 (Island lifespan)

On Unstable Islands with Index 2 or higher, every crater becomes a resource cache — 10 natural resources of one kind around the crater (5-tile radius), guarded by 3 animals that are ×1.5 tougher than normal (on top of the island's Index). The cache type depends on the island's climate, e.g. iron mine, rubber trees, fir forest · cache types and guards are re-rolled each time the island respawns.

Warp Accelerator A Rift is a crack in the ground leaking Warp energy. There are 4 per island (6 on Volcano islands) on Unstable Islands level 35–60 (except Deep Swamp), the temperate/tropical/tundra Civilized Islands, some event islands and the Lawless Islands (except the swamp one) — none on level 15–30 islands, Tamed Islands or the Safe House.

Tap an idle Rift → start the Warp Accelerator, paying the 1,000 T-Stone entry fee — everyone on the island gets an announcement Friends have 10 seconds to tap the Rift and join (also 1,000 T-Stones · within 10 tiles of the Rift · up to 10 players) Each tier, guard animals (the island's predators) appear around the Rift in 2 waves — clear them all within 60 seconds After a tier you get a 15-second break, then the next tier starts, up to 10 tiers · from tier 3, Allosaurus join the waves Run out of time = the run ends · tap the Rift to collect rewards within 2 minutes (once per player) · failing tier 1 = no reward The Rift then rests for 3 minutes before a new run can start Leaving the island or disconnecting mid-run removes you from the run — no reward for that run If starting/joining fails, your T-Stones are refunded Tier   Animals per tier (1 player)   Animals per tier (4 players) 1   3   5 3   5   9 5   7   12 10   12   20 Animals = (2 + tier) × (1 + 0.25 × (players − 1)), at most 20 per tier
